title: Cofinal monomorphisms of quasicategories are right anodyne
statement: Use the quasicategory, coherent comma, and weak-contractibility conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the right-anodyne class of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Let $j:A\hookrightarrow B$ be a degreewise injective map of small quasicategories, identifying $A$ with a full subcategory of $B$. For each vertex $b\in B$, form the coherent comma quasicategory $(b\downarrow j)=\{b\}\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_1}A$, retaining all higher simplices. If every $(b\downarrow j)$ is weakly contractible, then $j$ is right anodyne: it belongs to the class generated by the right horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$ under isomorphisms, pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts.

source.place: Remark 7.2.3.2 (02NZ), condition (2′), gives the right-cofinal criterion for exactly the displayed arrow-pullback comma; Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3) identifies right-cofinal monomorphisms with right anodyne maps. Theorem 7.2.3.1 (02NY) is the join-comma formulation. Equivalently HTT (April 9, 2017) Theorem 4.1.3.1, printed p.236, and Proposition 4.1.1.3(4), printed p.223, using the comma comparison. Online sources inspected; archive WANTED in report.md. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Apply (3)$\Rightarrow$(1) of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinality-space-test] to $u=j$. Its comma is exactly the arrow-pullback comma in the hypothesis, including higher simplices. Both indexing quasicategories are small in the stipulated universe. Thus restriction along $j$ preserves every given colimiting cocone in every containing target quasicategory. We use this conclusion with the opposite of a sufficiently large category of spaces; no colimits in $A$ or $B$ are required.

source.place: Remark 7.2.3.2 (02NZ), condition (2′), together with Proposition 7.4.3.11 (04K3), condition (2).

proof.text: Fix any small right fibration $q:Y\to B$. For $H=B,A$ write $q_H:H\times_B Y\to H$ and $\Gamma_H=\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(H,Y)$, with $H\to B$ equal to the identity or $j$. Pullbacks preserve the right-horn lifting property: compose a proposed square with the projection to $Y$, lift it for $q$, and pair the lift with its prescribed base simplex. Hence both $q_H$ are right fibrations. Apply [lem-coef-right-fibration-section-limit]: $\Gamma_B,\Gamma_A$ are Kan, and their evaluation cones are limits of $m_q:B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$ and $m_qj^{\mathrm{op}}$, respectively. Choose one containing universe for $Y,B$ and these spaces. The theorem's naturality under base restriction identifies the restricted evaluation cone with the cone induced by the actual simplicial restriction $r:\Gamma_B\to\Gamma_A$.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3), the section-space test; section/limit interpretation from HTT Corollary 3.3.3.4, opposite form.

proof.text: Regard $D=m_q^{\mathrm{op}}$ as a diagram $B\to\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$. Reversing simplices, with $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathscr C^{\mathrm{op}})$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,X^{\mathrm{op}})$ with endpoints exchanged, identifies the opposite of the cone category of $m_q$ in $\mathcal S$ with the cocone category of $D$ in $\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$. Terminal there is initial here: by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] applied to $X$ and to $X^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\operatorname{Map}_X(y,t)\simeq U_X(y,t)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{X^{\mathrm{op}}}(t,y)\simeq U_{X^{\mathrm{op}}}(t,y)\cong U_X(y,t)^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $|K^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|K|$, so one is contractible exactly when the other is. Hence the evaluation cone with vertex $\Gamma_B$ from Step 2 becomes a colimiting cocone on $D$; the same identification is used when reversing again below. Step 1 makes its restriction colimiting on $Dj$. Reversing again, the restricted evaluation cone with vertex $\Gamma_B$ is a limit of $m_qj^{\mathrm{op}}$. It and the evaluation cone with vertex $\Gamma_A$ are therefore terminal objects of the same coherent cone category of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. There is a morphism in each direction; their composites and the identities lie in the respective contractible mapping spaces into these terminal objects, giving inverse homotopies. Evaluating at the vertex shows that the induced comparison is an equivalence edge of $\mathcal S$; a $2$-simplex of the coherent nerve witnessing an inverse equation is an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(X,X)$, that is a simplicial homotopy, so the comparison is a simplicial homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. By the restriction compatibility in Step 2 this comparison is $r$ itself, so $r$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Empty section spaces cause no exception: if one has a vertex the equivalence forces the other to have one.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3): cofinality gives a homotopy equivalence on sections; expanded using the universal-colimit test and uniqueness of terminal cones.

proof.text:
The monomorphism clause of [lem-coef-unstraightening-homotopy-descent-gluing] applied over $S=B$ makes the same $r$ a Kan fibration. Together with Step 3 it is a trivial fibration in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], hence lifts every boundary, including $\varnothing=\partial\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$. In particular every prescribed section over $A$ extends exactly over $B$.

Now consider any lifting square with left edge $j$, right edge a small right fibration $p:X\to S$, top $a:A\to X$ and bottom $g:B\to S$. Form $Y=B\times_S X$. The elementary pullback argument of Step 2 makes $Y\to B$ a right fibration; $B$ is a quasicategory, so its total space is also a quasicategory by filling an inner horn first in $B$ and then lifting it. The top map gives the section $(j,a)$ over $A$. Its exact extension, obtained above, projects to a map $B\to X$ which restricts to $a$ and lies over $g$. Thus $j$ has the left lifting property against every small right fibration, with arbitrary simplicial base $S$.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3), final lifting-square argument; right-handed version. Kan-fibration input is HTT Lemma 2.2.3.4; weak equivalence plus Kan fibration is also Kerodon Proposition 3.2.7.2 (00X1).

proof.text: Let $I$ be the countable set of right horns $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0<i\leq n$. Apply [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] to small simplicial sets with $\kappa=\aleph_0$. Here are the required hypotheses. Hom sets are small sets of compatible degreewise functions. Small colimits exist: take each degree's disjoint union modulo the diagram relations; operators descend, and compatible maps out are exactly a cocone, giving [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Pushout along an injection adds its complement degreewise without identifying old elements, so an $I$-cell chain consists of injections. Each horn is the union of finitely many representable faces. A map from it into a sequential union is specified by finitely many face images and their overlap equalities. Choose a common stage containing those images; the equalities hold at a common later stage. Equality of two such maps is detected at a common stage by the same finite argument. Thus these horn domains preserve the sequential colimits in the small-object hypothesis. The theorem now gives $j=pi$ with $i:A\to Z$ an $I$-cell map and $p:Z\to B$ lifting every right horn, that is, a right fibration.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3), reduction to lifting against right fibrations; small-object factorization expanded to verify the finite-domain hypothesis.

proof.text:
Use Step 4 on the square with top $i:A\to Z$, bottom $\operatorname{id}_B$ and right edge $p$. It supplies $s:B\to Z$ with $sj=i$ and $ps=\operatorname{id}_B$. Hence $(\operatorname{id}_A,s):j\to i$ and $(\operatorname{id}_A,p):i\to j$ are maps of arrows whose composite is the identity: $j$ is a retract of $i$.

Every $I$-cell map is right anodyne in the exact sense of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne]. Indeed, refine each pushout of a small coproduct of horns by well-ordering its indexing set and attaching the horns one at a time along their given maps; maps out of this successive attachment are exactly compatible maps out of the original coproduct pushout. At limit ordinals take the union. Concatenating these small refinements leaves a small continuous ordinal chain of pushouts of single right horns. Isomorphisms and transfinite-composition closure place its composite $i$ in the stated class, and retract closure then places $j$ in it. This proves the conclusion with the nonzero-index horn convention of the item.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3), lifting characterization concluded by the small-object retract argument.
